title: Intrinsically generated randomness is repeatable across experimental runs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intrinsically generated randomness is repeatable across experimental runs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If randomness in an experiment comes from intrinsic generation, then even the precise details of the random-looking behavior should be repeatable from one run to the next, because such behavior is robust to perturbations below a critical size, whereas randomness from the environment or from initial conditions should show little or no repeatability.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But what is remarkable is that if intrinsic randomness generation is the mechanism at work, then the precise details of the behavior can also be repeatable.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “The Intrinsic Generation of Randomness” (from p. 315), p. 323. Scope: carefully controlled experiments showing random-looking behavior

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Controlled repeated-run datasets can test selected systems and compare mechanism predictions. Existing public data seldom measure perturbations finely enough, and repeatability is not uniquely diagnostic of intrinsic randomness generation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use repeated runs with measured and tightly controlled initial conditions, align trajectories, and quantify exact or local-pattern reproducibility as perturbation size is varied. Compare with runs receiving controlled environmental noise and with deliberately varied initial states.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Deterministic chaos can make intrinsic dynamics nonrepeatable after tiny perturbations.

Unmeasured environmental inputs can mimic intrinsic sensitivity.

Microscopic state cannot usually be reset exactly.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.62

analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Repeatability of details across runs is a sharp contrast among the three mechanisms, and the continuous-automaton perturbation pictures show what the threshold test would look like. The text says there is very little good information on natural experiments of this kind, and no public dataset now supplies matched raw repeats with measured perturbations. The criterion is ready; the observations it needs are not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat a controlled experiment below a measured perturbation threshold and test whether the detailed random-looking series agrees across runs. Stable details support intrinsic generation; run-to-run disagreement at the same detail level supports an environmental or initial-condition source.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw repeats of random-looking experiments are rarely deposited.

Perturbation size is seldom measured in the same run as the pattern.

Coarse agreement can be mistaken for detail-level repeatability.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.62

analysis feasibility: 0.28
